data.standardized_narrative: The syndicate experienced a gross release of GBP 63.926 million in prior year reserves, representing a 47.02% favourable movement against the opening gross claims outstanding. This favourable development is supported by narrative statements indicating robust technical provisions and improvements in reserves for both the 2014 and 2015 years of account. Despite this overall release, the report notes that claims experience for the 2015 Year of Account was higher than in recent years due to various catastrophe events and large losses, particularly affecting the Property and Aviation accounts.
raw_causal_phrases: Favourable movements of GBP 22.2 million, (2015: GBP 25.4 million), in the past year's provision for claims outstanding and IBNR, net of expected reinsurance recoveries
The technical provisions set at 31 December 2015 have proven to be robust, and there has been an improvement in reserves of around GBP 4.6m in the calendar year.
In 2016 there has been an improvement of GBP 10.3m on closed year reserves, which makes up the largest proportion of the result.

data.data_quality_notes: The report contains conflicting prior year development figures. The figure used for 'prior_year_development_gbp_m' is from the 'Technical provisions' reconciliation table on page 25, which is considered the most authoritative source for gross balance sheet movements. Other figures in the report (e.g., from page 2 and page 22) are different and may represent different accounting concepts (e.g., P&L impact or net figures). The 'prior_year_events' list includes events that occurred in the current report year (2016) but are explicitly stated to impact a prior year of account (2015 YOA), as per the report's narrative.
